title: Minimax Theorem From Loomis Theorem
body_html:
Minimax Theorem From Loomis Theorem

Loomis' theorem implies the finite von Neumann minimax theorem by taking $B$ to be the all-ones matrix. If $B_{ij}=1$ for all $(i,j)$, then for every mixed row $x\in\Delta(I)$ and every mixed column $y\in\Delta(J)$, $$ xB=(1,\ldots,1),\qquad By=(1,\ldots,1)^T. $$ The Loomis inequalities become $$ xA\ge v(1,\ldots,1),\qquad Ay\le v(1,\ldots,1)^T. $$ Equivalently, $$ xAy'\ge v \quad\text{for all }y'\in\Delta(J), \qquad x'Ay\le v \quad\text{for all }x'\in\Delta(I). $$ Thus $x$ guarantees $v$ for player 1 and $y$ guarantees $v$ for player 2, so the maxmin and minmax values coincide at $v$.

This node records the reverse direction from Loomis to minimax. The node zero_sum.minimax.loomis_theorem records the MFoGT proof route from minimax to Loomis, so the two nodes together document the equivalence discussed in MFoGT Section 2.5.
